label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.48 a.3…: There is EVIL_1 in a thing exactly when it lacks a…
locator: I q.48 a.3 co.: remotio boni privative accepta, malum dicitur
interpretation: Both directions are stated: privative removal of good is called evil, and negative removal (a man's lacking a deer's speed) does not have the nature of evil. 'Due' renders the privative sense: the subject is apt to have the good. The respondeo opens by recalling q.48 a.1 ('malum importat remotionem boni'), where evil is shown to be no nature but an absence of good; that article is not pinned separately. The subject of the privation being a being in potency is not formalized.
